description: Understand the architecture of modern high-performance computing systems. Analyze parallelism in computational problems. Design efficient shared-memory and distributed-memory parallel programs. Optimize applications for multicore CPUs and GPUs. Evaluate the performance and scalability of HPC applications. Apply HPC techniques to solve scientific and engineering problems.

syllabus.title: Introduction to High Performance Computing
syllabus.body: Evolution of HPC, need for and applications of HPC, Flynn's taxonomy, parallel computing models, types of parallelism, HPC system architecture, multicore and many-core processors, memory hierarchy, performance metrics, speedup, efficiency, scalability, Amdahl's law, Gustafson's law.

syllabus.title: Parallel Computer Architecture and Programming Models
syllabus.body: Shared memory systems, distributed memory systems, cluster computing, NUMA architecture, cache coherence, interconnection networks, parallel programming paradigms, thread-based programming, data and task parallelism, SIMD, MIMD architectures, introduction to OpenMP, directives, parallel regions, synchronization, work sharing constructs.

syllabus.title: Distributed Computing using MPI
syllabus.body: Message passing model, MPI architecture and environment, point-to-point and collective communication, communicators and groups, process topologies, non-blocking communication, parallel I/O, synchronization techniques, parallel algorithms using MPI.

syllabus.title: GPU Computing and Performance Optimization
syllabus.body: Introduction to GPU architecture, CUDA programming model, CUDA memory hierarchy, kernel programming, thread organization, memory optimization, load balancing, vectorization, loop optimization, cache optimization, performance profiling, benchmarking, parallel debugging tools.

outcomes: Understand the architecture of high-performance computers and how it affects program speed.
Understand how memory access affects the speed of HPC programs.
Understand Amdahl's law for parallel and serial computing and the importance of communication overhead.
Understand the general types of parallel computers and which types of problems suit each.
Understand practical aspects of message passing on MIMD machines.
referenceBooks: Thomas Sterling, Maciej Brodowicz, and Matthew Anderson, High Performance Computing: Modern Systems and Practices.
David B. Kirk and Wen-mei W. Hwu, Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach.
Ananth Grama, Anshul Gupta, George Karypis, and Vipin Kumar, Introduction to Parallel Computing.
